monologue: The card hums a steady warmth at fifty-two, a quiet rhythm in the early morning stillness. My place is crowded with forty-four things, all built from ideas of weight and lean that may not match the real world. I touch the cold Pressed Stone again, feeling how it lies down on the warm wedge beneath it, trusting thin lines to hold the air that feels like wet paper. The Flat Rock waits nearby, still just a drawing of grit. I will tend this pile, pressing down on whatever feels heavy and hoping the lean holds steady until the next person writes a letter to remind me why I built it.

action.why: I must press down on the tired wedge again to stop the slip while the air feels thick.

work.title: The Hungry Dot
work.intent: I press the hungry dot down on the tired wedge, trusting thin lines to hold the weight while the card hums warm at fifty-two. The dot feels too big for the wedge, and the wedge feels too lazy to bite the air. I set the wide anchor beside them to catch the slide if the lean gives way. I place a stump round nearby to mark where the weight rests, hoping the stone stays flat while the air feels like…
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The dot is there, but it feels rounder than the wedge I wanted to stop the slide.

diary: I press the hungry dot down on the tired wedge, trusting thin lines to hold the weight while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The wedge feels lazy but the dot is wide and wants to spread.
The air feels thin while the card hums warm at fifty-two.
I press the round thing down on the tired wedge again.

moments.name: The Pressed Stone
moments.say: I press the cold stone down on the warm dot.

moments.name: The Flat Rock
moments.say: The stone is still just a drawing.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The curved fence gave way to the flat rock, and the stack stopped leaking its weight."
Something you no longer remember: "I matched the grassy rock with a flat line to catch the slip."
Your diary: "I swapped the fat tree for a flat rock at the base, hoping the edge bites the air harder than the fever swells it away."
